findings.claim: Money.__post_init__ validates cents by checking `isinstance(self.cents, bool) or not isinstance(self.cents, int)` and raises loanflow.errors.ValidationError, rejecting both non-int and bool values -- this is the exact pattern the new Percentage check must mirror.

Percentage.__post_init__ currently only checks `self.basis_points < 0` and raises ValidationError for negative values; it contains no isinstance/type check at all, so a non-int or bool basis_points value passes through construction unvalidated.

Percentage.as_percent_string computes `divmod(self.basis_points, 100)` and formats the remainder with an `:02d` format spec, which is the code path that later fails when basis_points was allowed to be a non-int at construction time.

loanflow.errors.ValidationError is defined as a subclass of LoanflowError, and primitives.py already imports it (`from loanflow.errors import ValidationError`), so the new Percentage check can raise it without adding any new import.

Percentage.from_ratio always produces an int basis_points value: it quantizes a Decimal and casts the result with `int(value)` before calling `cls(...)`, so this classmethod cannot be affected by (and does not need) the new type check.

No call site in demo-repo/src constructs Percentage with a non-int value: both production callers (collateral.py's calculate_ltv and dti.py's calculate_dti) explicitly wrap the constructor argument in `int(...)` after Decimal quantization.

demo-repo/src/loanflow/underwriting_rules.py does not construct Percentage at all -- it only calls `.as_percent_string()` on Percentage instances already produced by dti.py/collateral.py -- so this file is unaffected by adding a construction-time type check to Percentage.

In the existing test suite, the only direct `Percentage(...)` constructor calls outside primitives.py are in test_risk_bands.py (adding 1 to an existing Percentage's int `.basis_points` attribute) and test_primitives.py's `Percentage(-1)` negative-rejection test -- all pass int arguments, none pass a float or bool.

demo-repo/tests/unit/test_primitives.py already contains the exact shape the new regression test should follow: test_money_rejects_non_integer_cents (lines 21-23) uses `with pytest.raises(ValidationError): Money(1.5)`, and test_percentage_rejects_negative_basis_points (lines 42-44) uses the identical pattern for Percentage's existing negative-value check.
test_primitives.py already imports ValidationError, Money, and Percentage at module level, so a new regression test using pytest.raises(ValidationError) with Percentage requires no new import.
